items.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Basie’s band was built around Herschel and Lester... I remember we had a battle of music with Benny Goodman one time... we had Al Killian, myself, Buck Clayton and Ed Lewis.

ctx.x: Did you ever feel after one of these trips and you’d stagger into a town, did you ever have to drag yourself onto the bandstand to do a show?

No, couldn’t wait, couldn’t wait to get onto the bandstand. Because Prez had as many favorites as Basie, his audience was just as big as Basie’s audience. Jo Jones, his audience was just as big as Basie’s, Buck had quite a following, Herschel Evans had quite a following. And Earl Warren had a pretty good following because he made a couple of good records singing. But put them all together, they drove (a) big crowd.
So you were treated as celebrities by the people coming to hear the band?

items.title: 68427_Harry Edison oral history interview
items.q: Herschel and Jo, they recommended me to Basie and I took his place... I joined Basie... Herschel died right after I got with the band

ctx.x: Most of the time he was playing alto?
Right. Alto and baritone. See, they had Earl Warren, they had Jack Washington, Herschel and Lester.
